directive.quote: Every engine job of the old Worker's rust-engine backlog rows works on the new engine, one to one or better.

preserve: one kept deletion per account, begun once; asking again while it is kept continues it, and a complete one is refused account_erasure_complete and never run again (beginAccountErasure)
bounded steps in a fixed order, tool runs first and the sign-ins last, each kept with its step and cursor after every page so a stop resumes at the page it was on (continueAccountErasure)

a failing step never parked: failure_delays_ms up to maximum_consecutive_failures, then the same failure waits repeat_growth times longer up to a week; a passing failure waits transient_delays_ms and never counts; a page that moves nothing stalls and waits longer (armAccountErasure)
a failure kept by its step and its words with every identifier taken out (deletionFailureShape)
the deletion's state read with times, counts, step and failure shape, never an identifier (accountErasureState)
a waiting deletion made due now with its failures, step and cursor kept (redriveAccountErasure)
nothing else of the account answers while its deletion is kept (accountBeingDeleted)

deleting needs a recent sign-in, a known passkey's confirmation for exactly this change on an account that has one, and on one with none a notice wait asked again after it, which a cancel ends (account/delete, delayedChange, cancelDelayed)
the account's files leave through the account files' own set-aside, forget and byte release, and its records through the record store's own destruction
allowed_deltas: the identity, share index, app state, born account, published item, host resource, raw export and shared network command steps, their quota permits, metadata retirement, policy-update fence carry, relay upgrade and superseded deletion are dropped: they are worker-host Durable Object parts; this engine keeps an account only in its own state folder
the alarm that drove the deletion with no caller is dropped (an always-on default): each delete-account call takes the next bounded steps and says when it may try again
the deletion and its continuation are one row in the account's own sign-in lists, written compare-and-set, instead of two Durable Object keys
the retry rule stamp and the platform's transient words are dropped: a step says itself that its failure passes
the operator's redrive is the person's own, sign-in:deletion with redrive
a recent sign-in at the door is a passkey confirmation made now for exactly this change, or a browser session ways::may_change admits; a personal key alone is not one
payment, camera, share owner and app installation clean-up of deleteAccount are product features and are left out
banned_substitutions: a step that erases another owner's rows other than through that owner's own functions
a deletion run without a recent sign-in, or twice
a central shared store of deletions
